blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **The Bill Behind an Accepted Repair**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol III, Agent Economics, § The Bill Behind an Accepted Repair
blocks.md: A team running the repair agent (a later section) is offered a model whose tokens cost a tenth as much. On the provider's invoice the switch looks like a large saving. In the team's own accounts it can raise the price of every repair that ships. The cheaper model may need more turns to reach a passing patch, and each turn holds a sandbox open and invokes tools.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Cohort cost per accepted task matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Measured cost per accepted task is the sum of every initiated task's account, each charge in exactly one category, divided by the distinct tasks accepted under one declared contract.

questions.q: The section **The Bill Behind an Accepted Repair** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Owning capacity beats an API at a delivered utilization u* = F / (3600 R (P_eff - v)), not at a token price.
A speedup g applied to a fraction f of the measured critical path gives T' = T[(1-f) + f/g] and a ceiling of 1/(1-f), which a baseline profile reveals before anything is bought.
Measured cost per accepted task is the sum of every initiated task's account, each charge in exactly one category, divided by the distinct tasks accepted under one declared contract.
A one-time adaptation investment recovers its cost after N* = C_adapt / (C_base - C_adapted) tasks, never if the per-task saving is nonpositive, and only while acceptance stays equal.
questions.hint: Re-read the excerpt and the section map: which idea is this section building toward?
questions.explanation: This section develops **Cohort cost per accepted task**: Measured cost per accepted task is the sum of every initiated task's account, each charge in exactly one category, divided by the distinct tasks accepted under one declared contract.

questions.q: True or false: in the book's concept map, *Cohort cost per accepted task* counts only outcomes accepted under *Task acceptance contract*.
